requirements.title: A FLUSH statement has a unit-number form or flush-spec-list form
requirements.definition: A flush-stmt is FLUSH file-unit-number or FLUSH with a parenthesized flush-spec-list.

pending.flush-unit-number-form: Compile/run `FLUSH u` on a named external file after writing a known record; assert only successful status and later Fortran readback where separately positioned.
pending.flush-spec-list-form: Compile/run `FLUSH (UNIT=u, IOSTAT=ios)` in the same control; the syntax negative removes only the parentheses or list.

requirements.title: FLUSH specifiers include optional UNIT, IOSTAT, IOMSG, and ERR
requirements.definition: A flush-spec is optionally keyworded UNIT=file-unit-number, IOSTAT=stat-variable, IOMSG=iomsg-variable, or ERR=label.

pending.flush-unit-specifier-form: Compile conforming FLUSH controls using both `UNIT=u` and positional `u`; placement restrictions remain owned by C1245.
pending.flush-iostat-specifier-form: Compile/run FLUSH with IOSTAT initialized to a nonzero sentinel and assert only zero/nonzero status.
pending.flush-iomsg-specifier-form: Compile FLUSH with a character IOMSG variable prefilled with nonblank sentinels; no future fixture compares the text.
pending.flush-err-label-specifier-form: Compile FLUSH with ERR= to a same-scope branch target; the syntax negative deletes only the label operand.

pending.flush-written-data-available-to-other-pr: No portable oracle: the availability of Fortran-written data to other processes is explicitly processor dependent, so future tests must not require interprocess visibility or timing.
pending.flush-nonfortran-data-available-to-read: No portable oracle: availability to READ of data placed by non-Fortran means is explicitly processor dependent and depends on external mechanisms outside the Fortran program.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.5-12.9: termination of data transfer, WAIT, BACKSPACE, ENDFILE, REWIND and FLUSH (batch164). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds. Round 1 found the portable WAIT no-operation cases missing - WAIT with ID=0 (explicitly permitted by 12.7.2 p3) and with ID= omitted on an asynchronous connection with nothing pending must succeed with IOSTAT zero - and an ENDFILE position plan that used REWIND, destroying the state under test; ENDFILE is now observed by the BACKSPACE that 12.8.3 p2 requires before the next transfer, after which a READ must report IOSTAT_END. Seventeen numbered rules were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
